The archrandom interface was originally designed for x86
RDRAND/RDSEED for receiving random words into registers
one function to generate an int and another to generate a long. However
other architectures don't follow this.
On arm64
column2: the SMCCC TRNG interface can return between one and three

column1: longs. On s390
column2: the CPACF TRNG interface can return arbitrary amounts

column1: with four longs having the same cost as one. On UML
interface can return arbitrary amounts.
So change the api signature to take a ""max_longs"" parameter designating
the maximum number of longs requested
column2: and then return the number of

column1: longs generated.
Since callers need to check this return value and loop anyway
implementation does not bother implementing its own loop to try again to
fill the maximum number of longs. Additionally
pass in a constant max_longs parameter. Taken together
mean that the codegen doesn't really change much for one-word-at-a-time
platforms
